explanation_en: The pronominal idiom 'hacerse fuerte' means to fortify one's position, dig in, or consolidate power/resistance in a specific place. It is widely used in military, political, and protest contexts to describe a group securing a foothold to resist opposition. It can also be used metaphorically to describe someone standing firm on an opinion.

examples.en_text: The soldiers have fortified themselves in the castle, and it is difficult to get them out of there.
examples.target_text: Los soldados se han hecho fuertes en el castillo y es difícil sacarlos de allí.

examples.en_text: The opposition members have dug in in the north of the country.
examples.target_text: Los miembros de la oposición se han hecho fuertes en el norte del país.

examples.en_text: With the new campaign, these local brands have established a strong foothold in the national market.
examples.target_text: Con la nueva campaña, estas marcas locales se han hecho fuertes en el mercado nacional.

examples.en_text: The protesters have dug in in the main square and do not intend to leave.
examples.target_text: Los manifestantes se han hecho fuertes en la plaza principal y no piensan irse.

examples.en_text: In the second half of the match, the defenders dug in and didn't let any ball get past.
examples.target_text: En la segunda parte del partido, los defensas se han hecho fuertes y no han dejado pasar ningún balón.

examples.en_text: The rebels have fortified themselves in the mountains and control all the roads.
examples.target_text: Los rebeldes se han hecho fuertes en las montañas y controlan todas las carreteras.

explanation_en: This formal expression means 'under the protection of', 'under the cover of', or 'in accordance with' (when referring to laws or regulations). It is highly common in legal, political, and journalistic contexts. It carries a connotation of being shielded or authorized by a specific framework or entity.

examples.en_text: Under the new law, workers are entitled to more vacation days.
examples.target_text: Al amparo de la nueva ley, los trabajadores tienen derecho a más días de vacaciones.

examples.en_text: We stayed under the shelter of the trees until it stopped raining.
examples.target_text: Nos quedamos al amparo de los árboles hasta que dejó de llover.

examples.en_text: Many animals go out to look for food under the cover of night.
examples.target_text: Muchos animales salen a buscar comida al amparo de la noche.

examples.en_text: The research project was developed under the auspices of the university.
examples.target_text: El proyecto de investigación se desarrolló al amparo de la universidad.

examples.en_text: She grew up under the care of her grandparents in a small northern town.
examples.target_text: Creció al amparo de sus abuelos en un pequeño pueblo del norte.

examples.en_text: Pursuant to this contract, the company must cover all travel expenses.
examples.target_text: Al amparo de este contrato, la empresa debe cubrir todos los gastos de viaje.

explanation_en: This adverbial phrase means to act, speak, or treat information with extreme care and skepticism. While 'cautela' means caution, combining it with 'coger con' (to take with) is the Spanish equivalent of 'taking something with a grain of salt' or treating it carefully. It is very common in journalism when reporting unconfirmed or fluid statistics.

examples.en_text: You should take news from social media with a grain of salt.
examples.target_text: Debes tomar las noticias de las redes sociales con mucha cautela.

examples.en_text: The doctor recommended that he walk with great caution after the surgery.
examples.target_text: El médico le recomendó caminar con mucha cautela después de la operación.

examples.en_text: The company is investing in new projects with great caution due to the crisis.
examples.target_text: La empresa está invirtiendo en nuevos proyectos con mucha cautela debido a la crisis.

examples.en_text: She always takes her neighbor's advice with a grain of salt.
examples.target_text: Ella siempre acepta los consejos de su vecino con mucha cautela.

examples.en_text: We had to move along the forest path with great caution because it was dark.
examples.target_text: Tuvimos que avanzar por el sendero del bosque con mucha cautela porque estaba oscuro.

examples.en_text: Both countries are negotiating the new trade agreement with great caution.
examples.target_text: Los dos países están negociando el nuevo acuerdo comercial con mucha cautela.

explanation_en: This expression means to examine or observe something closely or in detail, rather than from a distance. It can be used literally (looking at an object nearby) or figuratively (analyzing a situation or phenomenon thoroughly). It is a very common collocation with verbs like 'mirar', 'ver', or 'analizar'.

examples.en_text: I want to see the painting up close to appreciate all the details.
examples.target_text: Quiero ver el cuadro de cerca para apreciar todos los detalles.

examples.en_text: The director closely follows the work of the entire team.
examples.target_text: El director sigue de cerca el trabajo de todo el equipo.

examples.en_text: I don't know my new neighbor closely, but he seems very friendly.
examples.target_text: No conozco de cerca a mi nuevo vecino, pero parece muy amable.

examples.en_text: You have to look at the map closely to find that very small street.
examples.target_text: Tienes que mirar el mapa de cerca para encontrar esa calle tan pequeña.

examples.en_text: She has closely experienced the hospital's problems because she is a nurse.
examples.target_text: Ella ha vivido de cerca los problems del hospital porque es enfermera.

examples.en_text: I had never seen a lion up close and to be honest it scared me a little.
examples.target_text: Nunca había visto un león de cerca y la verdad es que me dio un poco de miedo.

explanation_en: This figurative expression is used to indicate that a situation, concept, or problem exceeds certain limits or has deeper implications than initially apparent. It is a staple of analytical and argumentative Spanish, helping to elevate the discourse when discussing complex topics.

examples.en_text: This new technology goes far beyond what we imagined ten years ago.
examples.target_text: Esta nueva tecnología va mucho más allá de lo que imaginábamos hace diez años.

examples.en_text: Our friendship goes far beyond sharing the same workspace.
examples.target_text: Nuestra amistad va mucho más allá de compartir el mismo espacio de trabajo.

examples.en_text: The impact of their music goes far beyond their most popular songs.
examples.target_text: El impacto de su música va mucho más allá de sus canciones más populares.

examples.en_text: A good teacher goes far beyond simply teaching the book's theory.
examples.target_text: Un buen profesor va mucho más allá de simplemente enseñar la teoría del libro.

examples.en_text: The ecological problem goes far beyond recycling plastic at home.
examples.target_text: El problema ecológico va mucho más allá de reciclar el plástico en casa.

examples.en_text: Taking care of mental health goes far beyond not being stressed at work.
examples.target_text: Cuidar la salud mental va mucho más allá de no estar estresado en el trabajo.

explanation_en: This expression means to anticipate or foresee an event or consequence. When negated ('no ver venir'), it indicates being caught completely off guard by a development. It is highly common in both casual conversations and analytical commentary.

examples.en_text: The storm started suddenly; we really didn't see it coming.
examples.target_text: La tormenta empezó de repente; realmente no la vimos venir.

examples.en_text: Their decision to get divorced was a surprise; we didn't see it coming at all.
examples.target_text: Su decisión de divorciarse fue una sorpresa; no lo vimos venir para nada.

examples.en_text: The success of our new product was something we didn't see coming.
examples.target_text: El éxito de nuestro nuevo producto fue algo que no vimos venir.

examples.en_text: The end of the movie was incredible; we really didn't see that twist coming.
examples.target_text: El final de la película fue increíble; de verdad no vimos venir ese giro.

examples.en_text: We ran out of funds very quickly; it was a problem we didn't see coming.
examples.target_text: Nos quedamos sin fondos muy rápido; fue un problema que no vimos venir.

examples.en_text: When Juan resigned from his job, we were all surprised; we didn't see it coming.
examples.target_text: Cuando Juan renunció a su trabajo, todos nos sorprendimos; no lo vimos venir.

explanation_en: Used to assert that a characteristic is inherently part of the nature or definition of a concept. It is a formal yet common logical connector used to strengthen an argument or clarify a fundamental truth about a subject.

examples.en_text: An equilateral triangle has, by definition, three equal sides.
examples.target_text: Un triángulo equilátero tiene, por definición, tres lados iguales.

examples.en_text: Art is, by definition, something subjective that depends on the viewer.
examples.target_text: El arte es, por definición, algo subjetivo que depende del espectador.

examples.en_text: A leader, by definition, must know how to listen to their team.
examples.target_text: Un líder, por definición, debe saber escuchar a su equipo.

examples.en_text: Social networks are, by definition, spaces to interact with others.
examples.target_text: Las redes sociales son, por definición, espacios para interactuar con otros.

examples.en_text: A surprise is, by definition, something you don't expect.
examples.target_text: Una sorpresa es, por definición, algo que no te esperas.

examples.en_text: Non-renewable resources, by definition, run out over time.
examples.target_text: Los recursos no renovables, por definición, se agotan con el tiempo.

explanation_en: Derived from shooting terminology, this idiom means to lose focus, get sidetracked, or miss the main point of a discussion. It is often used in conversational contexts when a speaker realizes they have digressed from the primary topic and want to steer the conversation back.

examples.en_text: I think that with this new proposal we are straying a bit off course from our initial objective.
examples.target_text: Creo que con esta nueva propuesta desviamos un poco el tiro de nuestro objetivo inicial.

examples.en_text: We started talking about vacations and got a bit off track from the meeting's topic.
examples.target_text: Nos pusimos a hablar de las vacaciones y desviamos un poco el tiro del tema de la reunión.

examples.en_text: If we only focus on the price, we are straying a bit off course from what really matters: quality.
examples.target_text: Si nos enfocamos solo en el precio, desviamos un poco el tiro de lo que realmente importa: la calidad.

examples.en_text: In the last report we got a bit off track and didn't answer the main question.
examples.target_text: En el último informe desviamos un poco el tiro y no respondimos a la pregunta principal.

examples.en_text: Sometimes we get a bit off track when we try to explain too many things at once.
examples.target_text: A veces desviamos un poco el tiro cuando intentamos explicar demasiadas cosas a la vez.

examples.en_text: At the end of last year, we strayed a bit off course with the project expenses.
examples.target_text: Al final del año pasado desviamos un poco el tiro con los gastos del proyecto.

explanation_en: A very common filler phrase and discourse marker used to call for attention, introduce an explanation, or express skepticism or evaluation of a situation. It helps structure spoken Spanish by signaling that the speaker is about to analyze or clarify a point.

examples.en_text: Let's see what the weather is like tomorrow before organizing the trip.
examples.target_text: Vamos a ver qué tiempo hace mañana antes de organizar la excursión.

examples.en_text: He says he is going to change jobs, but we'll see if it's true.
examples.target_text: Dice que va a cambiar de trabajo, pero vamos a ver si es verdad.

examples.en_text: Let's look at the options we have to solve this problem.
examples.target_text: Vamos a ver las opciones que tenemos para resolver este problema.

examples.en_text: Let's see, can you explain to me again how this program works?
examples.target_text: Vamos a ver, ¿me puedes explicar otra vez cómo funciona este programa?

examples.en_text: I have sent the email and now let's see if they reply to me today.
examples.target_text: He enviado el correo y ahora vamos a ver si me responden hoy.

examples.en_text: Let's see if the teacher gives us more time to finish the project.
examples.target_text: Vamos a ver si el profesor nos da más tiempo para terminar el proyecto.

explanation_en: An idiomatic phrase meaning to suffer damage, lose, or end up in a disadvantageous position as a result of a situation, conflict, or decision. Its opposite is 'salir bien parado' (to come out unscathed or successful). It is widely used in both formal and informal registers.

examples.en_text: If we decide to compete against that big company, we are going to come off very badly.
examples.target_text: Si decidimos competir contra esa gran empresa, nosotros vamos a salir muy mal parados.

examples.en_text: The ministers came off very badly from the last television interview.
examples.target_text: Las ministras salieron muy mal paradas de la última entrevista en televisión.

examples.en_text: The car crashed into a wall and, although the driver is fine, the vehicle came off very badly.
examples.target_text: El coche chocó contra un muro y, aunque el conductor está bien, el vehículo salió muy mal parado.

examples.en_text: Don't get involved in your friends' problems or you are going to come off very badly.
examples.target_text: No te metas en los problemas de tus amigos o vas a salir muy mal parado.

examples.en_text: The visiting team's players came off very badly after yesterday's match.
examples.target_text: Los jugadores del equipo visitante salieron muy mal parados tras el partido de ayer.

examples.en_text: She tried to defend her project alone, but she came off very badly in front of the bosses.
examples.target_text: Ella intentó defender su proyecto sola, pero salió muy mal parada frente a los jefes.

explanation_en: Literally meaning 'to hand over the bill', this figurative expression means that past actions, mistakes, or excesses eventually catch up with someone, resulting in negative consequences or a 'price to pay'. It is commonly used when discussing health, societal trends, or personal decisions.

examples.en_text: Staying up late so much during the week eventually takes a toll on your body.
examples.target_text: Trasnochar tanto durante la semana al final le pasa factura a tu cuerpo.

examples.en_text: The constant stress at the office is already taking a toll on her mental health.
examples.target_text: El estrés constante en la oficina ya le está pasando factura a su salud mental.

examples.en_text: The lack of physical preparation took its toll on us in the final minutes of the match.
examples.target_text: La falta de preparación física nos pasó factura en los últimos minutos del partido.

examples.en_text: Making so many mistakes at the beginning of your career can take its toll on you in the future.
examples.target_text: Cometer tantos errores al principio de tu carrera te puede pasar factura en el futuro.

examples.en_text: The excesses of youth always end up taking their toll over the years.
examples.target_text: Los excesos de la juventud siempre acaban pasando factura con los años.

examples.en_text: Those lies took their toll on him, and now he has lost his friends' trust.
examples.target_text: Esas mentiras le pasaron factura y ahora ha perdido la confianza de sus amigos.

explanation_en: This phrase is used to mean 'in the absence of' or 'lacking' something. It is a very common transition in news and formal writing to introduce a caveat or a temporary state before something is finalized. It can also be used in everyday speech to mean 'for want of' (e.g., 'a falta de pan, buenas son tortas').

examples.en_text: In the absence of lemon, we can use a bit of vinegar for the salad.
examples.target_text: A falta de limón, podemos usar un poco de vinagre para la ensalada.

examples.en_text: For lack of a better idea, we decided to stay home and watch a movie.
examples.target_text: A falta de una idea mejor, decidimos quedarnos en casa a ver una película.

examples.en_text: The project was canceled for lack of budget.
examples.target_text: El proyecto se canceló a falta de presupuesto.

examples.en_text: With five minutes left in the game, the score was still tied.
examples.target_text: A falta de cinco minutos para el final del partido, el marcador seguía empatado.

examples.en_text: For lack of available hotels, we had to sleep in a youth hostel.
examples.target_text: A falta de hoteles disponibles, tuvimos que dormir en un albergue juvenil.

examples.en_text: In the absence of an official response, people began to make up their own theories.
examples.target_text: A falta de una respuesta oficial, la gente empezó a inventar sus propias teorías.
